Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Canadian River at Amarillo 19N affecting Potter County.

is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Canadian River at Amarillo 19N.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of Rosita Creek Flats Recreational
Area floods. Primitive campers and recreational vehicles are in
imminent danger. Dirt roads that lead to highway 287 from Rosita
Creek Flats are impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 8.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.

at 3:30 AM CDT Wednesday was 8.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 10.0 feet this afternoon. It
will then fall tomorrow morning. It will rise to 8.4 feet early
Friday morning. It will then fall below flood stage early Friday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.4
feet on 06/01/2023.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 5:47PM CDT until October 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
The weather pattern on Wednesday will begin to change as an
approaching upper level low over the southwestern U.S. weakens the
subtropical ridge axis over Texas and the western Gulf. Isolated to
scattered showers and thunderstorms will develop during the daytime
hours. A Pacific cold front will move into the region Thursday
spreading showers and thunderstorms over more of the area. Rainfall
totals from Wednesday evening through Friday will be 2-4 inches with
isolated amounts up to 8 inches possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Texas, including the following
counties, Atascosa, Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet,
Caldwell, Comal, Dimmit, Edwards, Frio, Gillespie, Gonzales,
Guadalupe, Hays, Kendall, Kerr, Kinney, Llano, Maverick, Medina,
Real, Travis, Uvalde, Val Verde, Williamson, Wilson and Zavala.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is a potential for life threatening flooding
somewhere in the watch area. Excessive runoff may result in
flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and
flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall totals of 2-4 inches with isolated amounts of 8 inches
are possible.
